messages:
Jamal: Quick heads-up: during a pooling stress run I saw repeated badge-outs where low-priority tenants triggered slab demotes and blocked high-priority traffic briefly. p95 increased ~40ms.
Lina: Hmm. Is this the new shared-prefix arbitration or the older per-tenant slab split?
Jamal: Shared-prefix arbitration. Looks like evict permits are granted FIFO and a burst of low-priority prefills can hold the slab for ~80ms while they complete rehydrate+warmup.
Wei: We intended a tiny permit window (50ms) + priority-steal, but maybe long-running prefill tasks extend that. Any long-tail ops in the prefill path?
Carlos: Yes, cold prefill can hit model-loading paths that take up to 120ms in canaries. We should separate permit (short) from task lifetime (long).
Lina: Proposal: make permit a short-lived lease (e.g., 25ms) that only controls eviction ordering and not the full prefill lifecycle. After permit expiry, the prefill keeps running but no longer holds the eviction permit. High-priority steal can preempt future permits.
Wei: That avoids blocking eviction arbitration. But risk: two concurrent prefills touching same slab without permit could lead to double-rehydrate. Need a lightweight ownership token in slab metadata so only the first prefill writes back residency.
Jamal: Agreed. Ownership token = prefill_resident_id (uuid) stored atomically on first successful materialize. Prefill runner uses CAS to set token before write-back. Retries see token and become no-op.
Carlos: Also add a small metric: `prefill.permit_holders_by_priority` and `prefill.writeback_conflicts` so we can detect stray double-writes.
Lina: Another angle: prefetch backpressure at admission — if a slab has >N in-flight prefills, reject new low-priority attempts with a soft deny. N should be pool-sized, maybe 2. High-priority bypass allowed.
Wei: Let's define config knobs: permit_window_ms=25, max_inflight_prefills_per_slab=2, high_priority_bypass=true. Start canary with conservative values.
Jamal: For correctness, ensure demote marker + ownership token invariant: demote_epoch must increase on demote; prefill that set token for epoch X is valid only if slab.demote_epoch == X at writeback. Otherwise treat as stale and abort.
Carlos: Good catch. That prevents old prefills overwriting new state after a demote+rehydrate cycle.
Lina: Testing: unit for token CAS, integration where permit expires and a high-priority request steals permit, and chaos test with reordered writebacks. Also add alert: writeback_conflicts > 0.01% for 15m -> paged.
ops-bot: alert-rule-created: eng-runtime.prefill_writeback_conflict_rate warn=0.0001
Wei: I'll sketch the token CAS and admit/reject path. Jamal, can you produce the stress replay with mixed priorities? Carlos, patch metric names. Lina, you'll own canary rollout plan.
Jamal: Will do. Plan: roll to a single pool canary, run 12h with real traffic replay, validate p95/p99 for high-priority tenants. If green, expand.
Lina: TL;DR: separate short eviction permits from long prefill work, CAS ownership token at materialize, admission backpressure on low-priority, and metrics+alerts. I'll draft RFC note and a short runbook.
